title: Hinduism: Brahman, Atman and Karma
welcome_lead: Step into the rich world of Hinduism, the oldest of the major world religions.
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on Hindu beliefs in Brahman, atman, karma and dharma.
final_note: You can now explain Brahman, atman, karma and reincarnation in Hinduism.

walkthroughs.body_html: In Hinduism, Brahman is the one ultimate reality behind everything. Each person has an atman (soul) which is part of Brahman. The many Hindu gods are seen as different ways to picture and worship this one reality.
Karma means actions and their results. Good actions lead to good outcomes, bad actions to bad ones — in this life or future lives. Karma keeps the soul in samsara, the cycle of rebirth.
Dharma is your duty — to live morally and well, according to your role and stage of life. The ultimate goal is moksha: liberation from rebirth, when the atman unites with Brahman.

mcqs.q: Who do Sikhs consider their living guru today?
options: Sikhs follow a current living guru as their leader.
Sikhs consider the Dalai Lama their current guru.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
The Guru Granth Sahib — the Sikh scripture, declared the eternal guru by Guru Gobind Singh after the line of ten human gurus ended.

mcqs.q: What does natural law theory base morality on?
options: The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
Human nature and reason — there are objective purposes (telos) built into humans which reason can discover, generating universal moral precepts.
Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.
Natural law means whatever happens in nature is morally right.

mcqs.q: What does the Abrahamic covenant in Judaism involve?
options: The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
Sikhs consider the Dalai Lama their current guru.
Being 'chosen' means Jews believe they are superior to other peoples.
God's promise to Abraham of land, descendants and blessing, in return for faithfulness — the foundational covenant marking Jews as a covenant people with responsibilities, not privileges.
